score.about: OpenAI launched a beta Business Hub where you can claim your business listing in ChatGPT. Local businesses can only claim a listing that already exists, and claiming means accepting some terms you should read first.
score.gets: Something to do, useful but thin: go to chatgpt.com/business-hub and search your name; and a fact: by continuing you agree OpenAI's AI may call your business, and there is a covenant not to sue (the most interesting bit, buried in the middle).
score.stop: Maybe, for a second, on 'Your business in ChatGPT?'; the visuals add nothing.
score.leave_at: about 36 s, at 'But first, the small print': the one action (the address) came at 28 to 33 s, then it turns into terms reading with tiny strips; 'We searched ours, and it's not listed' at 51 s kills it
score.confused: whether a contractor counts as local; 'not listed ... offered to create one ... eligible online businesses' (can I make one or not); 'a dns record' never explained; the legal strips and most white strips too small to read; 'your listing person': who is that
score.comment: probably not; maybe 'So I give up my right to sue and their robot can call my shop? Pass.'
score.send: most likely nobody; maybe the one guy who handles our Google Business profile

reasons: point not whole by the end of the hook: 'no guarantee' and 'eyes open' arrive at 79 s; state it in the first 5 s
leaves at 36 s: start the steps by 8 s, cut the setup to one line, get to the terms fast (the line that holds a trades owner)
51 to 60 s 'We searched ours, and it's not listed' deflates it: say plainly what a local shop that is not listed can do
15 to 22 s: a contractor cannot tell if trades count: name trades or say how to find out
68 to 71 s 'a dns record': jargon; cut it or say it plainly
47 to 51 s legal strips too small: put the plain words big on the plate
strips throughout unreadable at phone size: one key line per screen, enlarged
85 s 'your listing person': say 'whoever runs your Google listing' on screen too
send fails: lead with the terms point; give one reason to check today without promising more recommendations
notes: 88 s is long for a four-step how-to
the character does the same wave and point throughout
too much text competing: plate, strip and caption at once
